title: Resolving abstract anaphors in Spanish discourse: Underspecification and mereological structures
research_question: How can hearers resolve an abstract anaphor when several individual propositions, events, or a merged multi-proposition discourse segment are all plausible antecedents?
methodology: The paper is primarily a theoretical and descriptive discourse-semantic study rather than an experimental evaluation. Zulaica analyzes Spanish discourse examples, including naturally occurring material from sources such as the Corpus de Referencia del Español Actual, by segmenting discourse into propositions and representing candidate antecedents as atomic and merged abstract referents. The analysis combines mereological representations inspired by the Justified Sloppiness Hypothesis with Segmented Discourse Representation Theory to model rhetorical relations and discourse topics. From these analyses the author proposes a hypothetical three-step cognitive resolution process, without testing it through a new psycholinguistic experiment or computational benchmark.

key_findings.finding: Abstract anaphors can be underspecified among multiple higher-order antecedents, including individual propositions, events, and larger multi-sentence discourse segments.
key_findings.section: 1 Introduction; 2 Discourse segments, abstract referents, and collective reference

key_findings.finding: The candidate set for an abstract anaphor can be represented mereologically so that atomic propositions and one or more merged complex abstract referents remain simultaneously available as possible interpretations.
key_findings.section: 1 Introduction; 3 Mereological structures and the Justified Sloppiness Hypothesis

key_findings.finding: The paper proposes a three-step resolution process: construct a mereological set of possible antecedents, infer rhetorical relations among its propositions, and select the preferred antecedent for the anaphor.
When several thematically connected propositions can be integrated into a coherent rhetorical unit, their merged interpretation is proposed to be preferred over its individual component propositions.
key_findings.section: 1 Introduction; 4 Propositional integration and rhetorical structure; 5 Conclusions

key_findings.finding: Rhetorical structure can determine proposition-level antecedent scope: a sequence connected by Continuation can form the merged referent of an anaphor while a nearby proposition connected by a different relation can remain outside that referent.
Narration and Continuation are proposed as especially conducive to forming merged discourse units, often functioning within a broader Elaboration relation to a discourse topic.
key_findings.section: 4 Propositional integration and rhetorical structure; 5 Conclusions

key_findings.finding: If no suitable rhetorical relation supports a merged interpretation, the proposed mechanism falls back to an atomic proposition in the candidate mereological structure.
key_findings.section: 1 Introduction; 4 Propositional integration and rhetorical structure

key_findings.finding: Discourse-topic construction is treated as incremental: new propositions can be integrated into an evolving complex segment rather than requiring an anaphor to link to only one immediately preceding proposition.

limitations: The central three-step resolution mechanism is explicitly presented as a hypothesis rather than as an experimentally validated cognitive model.
The study relies mainly on detailed analysis of selected discourse examples rather than a systematically sampled and quantitatively evaluated corpus of abstract-anaphor cases.
No new psycholinguistic experiment tests whether hearers actually prefer the predicted merged antecedents or follow the proposed processing sequence.
No computational resolver is implemented, so there are no accuracy, precision, recall, or baseline-comparison results.
The paper explicitly calls for future empirical psychological research on underspecification involving multi-sentence antecedents.
The role of discourse connectives and discourse markers in promoting mereological interpretations remains an open research question.
Differences among noun-phrase, pronominal, and demonstrative abstract anaphors in encouraging merged interpretations are left for future investigation.
The semantic ontology is intentionally simplified primarily to propositions and events rather than distinguishing finer categories of abstract objects.
The analysis concerns anaphoric reference rather than response acts, so it does not directly test approval, rejection, unanswered questions, or partial answers in workplace communication.
raw_claims: An abstract anaphor may have several propositions or events as plausible antecedents.
A sequence of propositions can itself constitute a complex abstract antecedent.
Atomic propositions and their merged interpretation can coexist in one candidate antecedent structure.
The proposed resolution process first keeps multiple interpretations available instead of forcing an immediate single-antecedent decision.
Rhetorical relations are used to decide whether propositions form a coherent merged discourse unit.
A merged interpretation is proposed to be especially salient when it represents a coherent general purpose of the speaker.
Continuation can join multiple propositions into a complex segment that an abstract anaphor subsequently denotes.
A proposition located near an anaphor need not belong to its antecedent if rhetorical structure places that proposition outside the relevant complex segment.
Discourse topics can be incrementally updated as further thematically related propositions are processed.
When no coherent merged referent can be constructed, an individual proposition remains available as the anaphor's antecedent.
The paper treats the three-step mechanism as a hypothesis and explicitly identifies empirical validation of multi-sentence antecedent resolution as future work.
